clue.text: Son needs to mature to become a wise man

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A boy has to grow up before he can be considered wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a person revered for profound wisdom, a synonym for a wise man.

clue.text: Quiet place of worship lacking energy and run down

parts.note: SH is the hushing call for quiet

indicators.note: lacking says the place of worship goes without the energy letter

parts.note: an abbey is a monastic church
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sleepy, neglected church with no life left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' is the hushing sound SH, not a description of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby is worn and dilapidated, the state of a building gone to seed.

clue.text: Possessing supposedly special knowledge costing bucks

indicators.note: a horse that bucks throws itself about, so the letters of costing are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Insider know-how that supposedly comes at a price in dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucks' reads as dollars but is a verb, jolting COSTING into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gnostics claimed secret, saving insight, so the adjective describes claiming esoteric wisdom.

clue.text: Christian supplier of medieval weaponry?

definitions.meaning: ... Christian led the mutiny on HMS Bounty
the question mark flags the loose description

explanation.surface: A religious believer who sells old weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' looks like a believer, but it is the mutineer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Bounty mutineer is also the trade name of an arrow maker.

clue.text: Style him 'Sir', feeble MP getting permanent entitlement to be in the club

definitions.text: permanent entitlement to be in the club

indicators.note: to style is to arrange or fashion, so the letters are refashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A weak politician, once knighted, is given lasting privileges at his gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' seems to mean give a title, but it rearranges HIM SIR FEEBLE MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifelong enrolment in a society grants a member indefinite rights there.

clue.text: Vulgar set? No — just a bit wet

definitions.text: set? No — just a bit wet
definitions.meaning: paint or glue that has not yet set is still slightly sticky

explanation.surface: Is the crowd coarse? No, merely a little soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both tasteless and still slightly sticky, as drying varnish is.

clue.text: Perhaps I'm fed up and settle finally in tall house

indicators.note: in says the final letter goes inside the word for tall

parts.note: tall means high

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of settle

explanation.surface: Someone weary and ready to settle down in a tall house at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from 'settle', and 'in' places it inside HIGH to give HEIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation voices boredom or resignation, so it stands for a sighed 'I'm fed up'.

clue.text: Liberated with some money being brought around

indicators.note: brought around means the currency is wrapped round the word some

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

explanation.surface: A hostage set free once a sum of cash is delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' is taken as written and placed inside RAND, the South African currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive bought back from kidnappers has been freed, the payment securing release.

clue.text: Wild beast sets everyone in conflict over nothing repeatedly

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the next
in places the word for everyone inside the word for conflict

parts.note: war is armed conflict
all means everyone

indicators.note: repeatedly means the zero letter is used twice

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An untamed animal stirs up a fight among everybody over nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This large kangaroo of rocky Australian country is a wild marsupial.

clue.text: Coat in shop — it is unusual in style

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters come out in an uncommon arrangement

explanation.surface: A shop coat is out of the ordinary and very chic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges COAT IN SHOP IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Refinement and elegance of manner are what is meant by style.

clue.text: A very old colleague of Quixote's about to have egg and fruit

indicators.note: about tells us the colleague's name is turned round

parts.note: Dac is another setter of the Independent crossword, alongside Quixote
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: An elderly companion of Don Quixote is about to eat egg and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Quixote is this puzzle's setter; 'about' reverses DAC, a fellow Independent setter, to give CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The pear-shaped green produce of a tropical tree is botanically a fruit.

clue.text: Female wants excitement in party group

parts.note: action means lively goings-on, excitement

explanation.surface: A woman looks for thrills inside her political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting bloc within a larger political party.

clue.text: Little woman joining the fellow in module in birthplace

parts.note: Beth March is one of the sisters in Little Women

indicators.note: in puts the fellow inside the module

parts.note: LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions
he is the fellow

explanation.surface: A small woman and a man meet up in a space capsule.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Judea is where Jesus was born, the archetypal birthplace.

clue.text: Crude person's exclamation of joy

definitions.meaning: a boorish lout, after the brutish humans in Gulliver's Travels

explanation.surface: A boor shouting with glee.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both Swift's term for a brute and a cry of delight.

clue.text: A choirmistress upset when losing one garden plant?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A choir leader gets upset after losing a single singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when losing one' removes I from A CHOIRMISTRESS before 'upset' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The hellebore that flowers in winter is a familiar border plant.

clue.text: Most frightening sign of injury that is seen on street

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound
IE abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A terrifying wound mark is visible out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of scary is a straightforward synonym for most terrifying.

clue.text: Fancy parcels around tree initially, having a range of colours?

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters sit round the tree's first letter
fancy as a verb means imagine, giving the letters an imaginative new order
initially picks the first letter of tree

explanation.surface: Elaborately wrapped presents under the Christmas tree look colourful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges PARCELS to SPECRAL, and 'around' wraps it round T from 'tree initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a band of colours, so spectral can mean relating to it; the query flags the other sense, ghostly.

clue.text: Seasonal character having a mad moment with pie being thrown

indicators.note: letters being thrown are flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Christmas-show figure goes wild while custard pies fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being thrown' rearranges A MAD MOMENT PIE. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; the dame is a man in comic drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-dressed comic lead appears in pantomimes over the Christmas season.

clue.text: Seat to accommodate four residents

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so four goes inside

parts.note: nates are the buttocks, one's seat
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A seat big enough for four people living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' is the backside, NATES, the anatomical Latin for buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are people born in a place and living there, its residents.

clue.text: Modern trader working in atelier

indicators.note: working means in operation, the letters set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A contemporary dealer is busy in an artist's studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ATELIER, a workshop or studio.
explanation.definitionFit: An online shop selling goods over the internet is a recent kind of merchant.

clue.text: Maiden in fairy tale possibly tempestuous

indicators.note: in puts the maiden's letter inside the tale

parts.note: a fairy tale is one kind of story, hence possibly
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl in a fairy tale might be wild and turbulent.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather full of gales and squalls is both stormy and tempestuous, a near synonym.

clue.text: Mentions things worth seeing to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: sights are attractions worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone tells listeners about attractions worth a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite something is to quote or refer to it, a synonym for mention.

clue.text: Resentful having caught cold in search

indicators.note: having caught means holding something inside

parts.note: sour means bitter and resentful
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A bitter person who has caught a chill is out looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly.

clue.text: Nasty Alsatians will suit aggressive person

indicators.note: nasty suggests a vicious turn, signalling the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: Vicious guard dogs will suit someone who likes to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' rearranges ALSATIANS, the British name for German shepherd dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is an attacker, someone who sets upon another.

clue.text: Food eaten by player, a violinist

indicators.note: eaten by means swallowed inside the following words

explanation.surface: A violinist in the orchestra wolfs down a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffed pasta squares are an Italian dish, so a kind of food.

clue.text: Man's man may be so isolated

definitions.meaning: a man from the Isle of Man is an islander

explanation.surface: A manly man may be cut off from others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's man' looks like a macho type, but Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means relating to an island and also narrow and cut off from outside influence.

clue.text: Desire by band to appear in glossy fabric

parts.note: lust is strong desire
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: Passion for a musical group shows up in a shiny cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustring is a lustrous silk dress material, a shiny textile.

clue.text: Loud man to become ragged in battle

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A noisy man's clothes become tattered in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also means to become ragged, a second sense the clue folds into its surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a brawl or fight, an old word for a battle.
